```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6)
```

```{r setup}
library(pam50)
```

`pam50` assigns breast-cancer samples to the five PAM50 intrinsic subtypes
(Basal, Her2, LumA, LumB, Normal) using the published Perou Lab centroids, with
optional Zhao4 subtype-specific normalisation, ROR-S/ROR-P risk scores, intrinsic
clustering and claudin-low identification. It is the exact algorithm used by the
Swarbrick Lab PAM50 pipeline — packaged, not reimplemented.

## An expression matrix in, calls out

The high-level entry point is `pam50_subtype()`. Here we use the bundled public
example (the Perou `PAM50_example` 200-subject matrix, whose rows are already the
classifier's gene identifiers, so we skip symbol mapping and Zhao normalisation):

```{r}
expr <- as.matrix(read.table(
  system.file("extdata", "example_expr_200.tsv", package = "pam50"),
  sep = "\t", header = TRUE, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE
))
dim(expr)

res <- pam50_subtype(expr, map_symbols = FALSE, zhao = FALSE, calibration = NA)
res
```

The result is a `pam50_result`. Inspect it:

```{r}
summary(res)
head(as.data.frame(res)[, c("Call", "Confidence", "ROR-S (Subtype Only)")])
```

## Visualisations

Per-subtype correlation and proliferation (the default `plot()` method):

```{r}
plot(res)
```

A training-vs-test PCA places the cohort against the reference set:

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("impute", quietly = TRUE)}
plot_pam50_pca(res)
```

## A typical real run

With a gene-symbol expression matrix and a sample sheet carrying clinical
(ER × HER2) subtype, the usual call enables symbol mapping and Zhao
normalisation (and optionally intrinsic clustering + claudin-low):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
res <- pam50_subtype(
  expr,                          # rows = HGNC symbols
  samples      = sample_sheet,   # has sample_id + clinical_subtype
  subtype_col  = "clinical_subtype",
  cluster      = TRUE            # adds Call_CLOW + $intrinsic
)
```

## Other input types

`pam50_subtype()` (and `pam50_run()` / `pam50_add_samples()`) also accept a
`SummarizedExperiment` / `SingleCellExperiment`, an `anndataR` `AnnData`, or a path
to an `.h5ad` file — the sample sheet is taken from `colData` / `obs`, and `layer=`
picks the assay/layer:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pam50_subtype(sce, layer = "log2_uqn")             # SummarizedExperiment / SCE
pam50_subtype("cohort.h5ad", layer = "log2_uqn")   # .h5ad (needs anndataR, R >= 4.5)
```

## Reference data and the command line

Bundled reference data is available directly: `pam50_centroids()`,
`pam50_annotation()`, `sigma_table()`, `intrinsic_genes()`. The same operations
are reachable from the shell via the `pam50` CLI (`pam50 classify`, `pam50 zhao`,
`pam50 cluster`).
